device: Laser gate tap: a copy of the RTC6 LASERON for the digitizer (the sync reference)
where (model part, module): 4U drawer: the RTC6 laser-connector breakout (ZL-RTB-DB15, C1)
bom line: C1 (adds a 10 kΩ resistor and a BNC)
signal type: digital, LASERON level (to confirm with SCANLAB)
connector: breakout terminal -> 10 kΩ -> BNC -> Pico BNC-to-D9 adapter (TA271 class: check its wiring)
notes: passive tap: 10 kΩ keeps a fault on the monitoring side from driving the IPG gate (L-04); the 50 % point lags 0.12 µs (RC ln 2), calibrated out. Every gate edge is known in RTC6 time, so the digitizer clock is fitted to them per layer

device: RTC6 digital out bit 0: camera window (set by a short list command when an imaged mark starts, cleared when it ends)
where (model part, module): RTC6 EXTENSION port -> 4U drawer terminals -> PB2
signal type: digital, TTL class (RTC6 levels and drive to confirm)
connector: RTC6 EXTENSION connector -> DIN breakout (type to confirm) -> M12 8-pin A-coded bulkhead on the guard (MN-28) -> PB2
cable: shielded 4-pair with MN-03 to MN-05, 2.5 m, shield at the drawer end only
notes: gates the frame bursts: first trigger a set delay after the edge, then a fixed period; restarting each mark bounds the generator's crystal drift (50 ppm x 70 ms = 3.5 µs)

device: RTC6 digital out bit 1: layer start (100 µs pulse with the layer's first command)
where (model part, module): as MN-02
controller: Pi 5 GPIO (through MN-21) and MN-21's time-tagger
notes: the Pi time-stamps it (kernel GPIO event) to tie each layer's RTC6 tick to UTC; the PLC log and the layer stills are on the Pi clock

device: RTC6 digital out bit 2: track toggle (flips at each mark start)
where (model part, module): as MN-02
notes: optional; the RTC6 log's output word records it too, so a missed edge can be found

device: RTC6 digital out bit 3: Chronos record end
where (model part, module): as MN-02, then PB2 -> the Chronos at the left-wall port
channel: TRIG3 (isolated input, Aux pins 7 and 8), Record End Trigger
cable: same cable to PB2, then a twisted pair 1 m
notes: the isolated input keeps the camera out of the signal ground; threshold about half the logic level (Kron: drive at about twice the threshold); debounce off

device: Coaxial camera trigger (monochrome IMX296 board)
where (model part, module): coaxial branch above the bridge (30 mm cage); MN-21 in PB2
signal type: digital, 1.8 V, active low: exposure = low pulse + 14.26 µs
connector: solder pads -> 2-pin JST-SH on a strain-relief tab
cable: twisted pair 0.4 m; 1.5 kΩ in series and 1.8 kΩ to GND at the camera (Raspberry Pi's divider from 3.3 V)
notes: remove R11 if Q2 is fitted, then echo 1 > /sys/module/imx296/parameters/trigger_mode (Raspberry Pi docs); fix gain and white balance or frames are dropped; trigger-to-exposure latency and jitter not published: measure (§1.5)

device: Coaxial camera data
where (model part, module): coaxial branch -> PB2
channel: CAM1 (CAM0 is the layer camera, P-07)
cable: Raspberry Pi camera cable <= 0.5 m (about 0.29 m straight from x -215 to PB2: check the route)
notes: a third CSI camera (the steep lid port, LP) needs a second Pi 5 or a USB3 camera

device: Chronos frame trigger (Exposure Trigger mode)
where (model part, module): MN-21 in PB2 -> the Chronos at the left-wall port (inside the guard)
notes: Kron: synchronised within 500 ns; the pulse rate must not exceed the frame rate set in the camera or frames drop; Shutter Gating if the pulse should set the exposure (>= 1 µs)

device: Chronos frame-sync output (high while the shutter is open)
where (model part, module): Chronos -> PB2
channel: GPIO in through a divider or opto
notes: commissioning, and any run where every frame must be accounted for

device: Chronos Gigabit Ethernet
where (model part, module): Chronos -> MN-28 -> machine switch (E2) or a NIC on the scan PC
notes: a 32 GB burst takes ~5 min at 110 MB/s: save between bursts, or to the camera's eSATA SSD

device: Chronos power
where (model part, module): Chronos; its AC adapter outside the guard on a UPS outlet
cable: adapter lead through MN-28's split cable entry
notes: a 24 V -> 19 V DC-DC on the CTRL rail would add 40 W (17 % of the SDR-240-24): the camera's own adapter is the simpler choice

device: Monitoring stop request -> RTC6 external stop (not safety-rated)
where (model part, module): Pi 5 GPIO -> RTC6 /STOP input
signal type: digital, active low for >= 10 µs (RTC4 manual; the RTC6 pin to confirm)
connector: laser-connector breakout (RTC4: /START and /STOP are on the laser connector)
notes: optional hardware path; the normal path is software (the scan PC calls the RTC6's stop). It aborts the list and turns the laser signals off. Not part of the safety chain, and it can only stop

device: Photodiode 1 Thorlabs PDA36A2 (T2): signal
where (model part, module): coaxial branch above the bridge -> MN-28 -> 4U drawer
signal type: analog 0-10 V into Hi-Z (5 V into 50 Ω); 260 kHz at 30 dB
connector: BNC -> isolated BNC bulkhead -> BNC -> BNC-to-D9 adapter
cable: double-shielded RG-223 (or RG-58), 3 m, in the signal duct, away from servo and heater cables
notes: replaces L-16's 'RTC6 analog in / DAQ': the RTC6 has no analog inputs (SCANLAB comparison table: two 12-bit analog outputs). Shield on the - input breaks the ground loop (60 dB CMRR to 1 MHz)

device: Photodiode 2 PDA36A2 (second band of the two-colour pair)
where (model part, module): as MN-13
notes: same gain as MN-13 so the two bands have the same bandwidth and delay

device: PDA36A2 power, x2
where (model part, module): Thorlabs LDS12B linear supplies outside the guard, on UPS outlets
notes: linear, so no switching noise at the detectors; check whether the LDS12B output is floating, so the detector grounds only through the cage

device: AE sensor (MISTRAS PICO, Ø5 x 4, on the waveguide's foot in a 316L cartridge inside the rod end; S25: a sensor strapped to its rod end's back face; monitoring/mechanics.md §4)
where (model part, module): inside the rod end's bore (M50, L75), in argon; moves with the piston and leaves with the module
cable: a gas-side Kapton coax pigtail on the weld-in's pin, an in-line 10-32 joint to the sensor's lead; outside, the weld-in's 10-32 plug to the preamp, <= 1-2 m
chamber feedthrough: Solid Sealing FA40102 Microdot weld-in in the rod end's cap (M4-13), laser or e-beam welded before the rod; unplugged at a swap like the other weld-ins
notes: isolate the sensor face from the module (isolated sensor or a ceramic wear plate) so the AE chain is grounded only at the digitizer; the module keeps its own bonding strap (electrical.md §8). Round 3 (2026-11-27): the sensor moved inside the rod end, under the waveguide (MN-27)

device: AE preamp: MISTRAS 2/4/6 (20/40/60 dB, 18-28 V on the signal BNC) or Vallen AEP5 (34/40 dB, 28 V on the signal cable)
where (model part, module): a bracket under the chamber floor, <= 1 m from the sensor, kept <= 65 °C (2/4/6 rating; AEP5 85 °C)
connector: BNC (signal and power on one coax)
cable: RG-58, 3 m, through an isolated BNC bulkhead
notes: 40 dB; band-pass 50-600 kHz in software (Seleznev 2022) or a plug-in 100-300 kHz filter on the 2/4/6

device: AE decoupler Vallen DCPL-24V-V1 (DIN): 28.5 V to the preamp, the AE signal out to the digitizer
where (model part, module): 4U drawer (DIN rail)
signal type: AE out, ±5 V max into >= 10 kΩ
cable: <= 5 m to the digitizer (Vallen); 0.5 m in the rack
notes: a MISTRAS 2/4/6 also runs on 28 V over its BNC; check the DCPL's current against the 2/4/6's 30 mA with Vallen

device: AE decoupler power
where (model part, module): 24 V CTRL rail -> MN-18
channel: a CBMC E4 channel shared with drawer loads
notes: Vallen found a switched supply added 13-15 dBAE of noise on the DCPL2: measure the floor with the pump and blower running, and fit a linear 24-28 V supply if it matters

device: PicoScope 4444 USB 3.0
where (model part, module): 4U drawer (or the rack's side) -> scan PC
cable: USB 3.0 A-B 1.8 m in the rack
notes: 190 x 170 x 40 mm; 4 ch x 2 MS/s = 16 MB/s through the SDK (ceiling 50 MS/s); ±50 ppm timebase, fitted to the RTC6 each layer

device: Trigger generator and time-tagger: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RP2350) on a screw-terminal carrier
where (model part, module): PB2 (the process-module box on the bridge)
signal type: 3.3 V logic; one output buffered to 5 V
voltage / current: USB 5 V from the Pi, < 0.1 A
notes: PIO: gated bursts started by MN-02, outputs MN-06 and MN-08, time-tags MN-02 to MN-04 and MN-09 at 150 MHz. Without firmware: a 2-channel function generator in gated-burst mode does the triggers but not the tags

device: Side-camera light: Thorlabs M850D3 850 nm LED imaged onto the plate by an ACL25416U-B asphere, strobed (monitoring/optics.md §4.1)
where (model part, module): outside the back-wall viewport BW, on an L bracket screwed to the back wall above the BW clamp frame
voltage / current: 0-2 A pulses from the driver's LED2 terminal (1.14 A mean at most); the driver on mains outside the guard
controller: own driver (Thorlabs DC2200 in TTL mode); strobe from MN-21
connector: the M850D3's board leads to CAB-LEDD1 / the driver's LED2 terminal
notes: an LED, not a laser: no laser controls, but RG3 in its own beam inside the chamber, so enable it only with the chamber door shut (the door switch in the driver's enable, or the Pico 2 holding the strobe low), or keep to <= 0.75 A CW with the door open; leave the board's EEPROM pins off the driver, which otherwise caps it at 1.5 A. Round 3 (2026-11-27): replaces the 808/850 nm light planned at LW

device: Second layer light (raking, behind the back-wall window BW)
where (model part, module): outside the back wall, on the window adapter
channel: a spare DO (30 of 32 used with it)
notes: fired in turn with P-08 for the stills; the Pi asks the PLC over Modbus; ms timing is enough for stills

device: RTC6 command log: the Ethernet data stream (StreamParser) or set_trigger4 each layer
where (model part, module): RTC6 Ethernet board -> scan PC
channel: a NIC of its own (direct cable, not through the machine switch)
notes: StreamParser: up to 8 channels, independent of the job, RTC6 software >= 1.16.3 (SCANLAB); set_trigger4: 4 channels x 2^23 values = 84 s at 10 µs; which head signals the basiCube 20 returns over SL2-100 is to confirm (no advanced diagnosis)

device: Pi 5 -> scan PC data link
where (model part, module): PB2 -> machine switch (E2) -> scan PC
notes: per-layer camera files (95-534 MB a layer, data_budget.md) move during the 8 s recoat at ~110 MB/s

device: Monitoring hold or stop request (software)
where (model part, module): scan PC monitor -> Pi supervisor (REST) -> RTC6 list, or a request bit to the PLC
notes: severity 2: hold before the next layer (the dwell mechanism); severity 3: stop the list on the RTC6 (not safety-rated). The PLC request bit can only make the PLC drop its own process permissive (S-12), never set it

device: AE waveguide (Ø3 mm 316 rod, Ø4 head domed R50) from the plate's spigot down the hollow rod to the sensor (MN-16)
where (model part, module): module (CAD)
chamber feedthrough: none: the waveguide stays inside the gas boundary, sprung up by a Lee LC 029BB 09S316 under the sensor; only the sensor's lead crosses, through MN-16's weld-in
notes: the rod end has been hermetic since round 5 (electrical.md §13.3) and has no straight way out, so round 3 (2026-11-27) put the sensor inside it: 13.3-16.8 N on the plate with the stop force shimmed at assembly; needs the bayonet's disc spring (monitoring/mechanics.md §4)

device: Monitoring bulkhead plate on the guard (new)
where (model part, module): the guard panel nearest the rack (CAD to place)
connector: 3 isolated BNC (MN-13, MN-14, MN-17), 1 RJ45 (MN-10), 1 M12 8-pin (MN-02 to MN-05), a split cable entry for pre-terminated leads (MN-11, MN-15)
notes: no line of sight through any opening (connectors and grommets), so the guard stays light-tight: show the LSO; bond the plate to the guard; isolated BNCs keep cable shields off the guard

device: Guard and PB2 fans: 2 x Delta AFB1224SH 120 mm (exhaust), 1 x AFB0624H-A 60 mm (the side camera's hood), 1 x Noctua NF-A4x10 24V 40 mm (PB2) (monitoring/cooling.md §6)
where (model part, module): the exhaust plenum outside the guard's back panel; the hood duct; PB2's +x end wall
controller: 24 V CTRL rail, on whenever the guard's devices are powered
connector: the fans' leads to DIN terminals in PB2 or the 4U drawer
cable: 2-core, through the guard bulkhead (MN-28) for the exhaust fans
notes: the guard's air runs 26-44 K over the Shuttle's without them; with them 5-10 K over its supply (monitoring/cooling.md §0). Round 3 (2026-11-27)
